title: Synapse
description: Sync latency, connections, gateway work, relay, API and process health. Generated by observability/build-dashboard.py.

panels.title: Open sockets
panels.description: People connected right now (WebSockets open on the gateways).

panels.title: Open documents
panels.description: Documents currently held in gateway memory (a room closes 5 s after the last person leaves).

panels.title: Relay (Redis)
panels.description: Whether gateways can see each other's edits. DOWN means people on different gateways are not seeing each other live; rooms repair themselves from the database when it returns. 'no data' means the server runs without Redis (single gateway).

panels.title: Rooms with unsaved edits
panels.description: Documents holding edits the database has NOT accepted. Should always be 0. Above 0 means the database is down or failing: people can still type, but a gateway crash now could lose edits (browsers still hold their copy).

panels.title: Connection success (5 min)
panels.description: Of the connections that finished, how many reached a synced state: synced / (synced + failed). 'Failed' means a connection that dropped by itself before syncing; attempts the browser cancelled (leaving the page) are not counted. This is the project's availability proxy; the target is 99.9%. 'no data yet' if no connection finished in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: API server errors (5 min)
panels.description: Share of API requests that failed with a 5xx error. Should be 0.

panels.title: Sync latency, as people feel it (measured in their browsers)
Round trip, browser to gateway and back
panels.description: Each browser asks the gateway to echo a timestamp every 5 seconds; this is how long that took. It covers the browser, the network and the gateway. Remote edits travel the same path, so this is the best proxy for 'how soon do others see my edit'. Red line: the 250 ms target. Includes any delay set in the network simulator. Each point looks back 1 minute.

panels.title: Keystroke to paint
panels.description: From pressing a key to the screen updating, measured in the editor (printable keys, about 10 samples a second at most). Red line: the 50 ms target. Each point looks back 2 minutes.

panels.title: Time to sync after (re)connecting
panels.description: From opening a connection until the document is fully synced (handshake complete). Rises when documents are large or the network is slow.

panels.title: How long people were offline
panels.description: After a lost connection, the time until the browser was synced again. Long values mean people were disconnected for a while (or used the offline simulator).

panels.title: Sockets and documents open
panels.description: How many people are connected and how many documents the gateways hold.

panels.title: Joins per minute
panels.description: Attempts to open a document. 'rejected' means the server refused (not signed in, no access, or a removed member).

panels.title: Browser connections per minute
panels.description: What browsers report: 'attempt' is every try (including ones the browser cancelled), 'synced' the ones that completed, 'failed' the ones that dropped before syncing.

panels.title: Reconnects per minute
panels.description: Browsers coming back after losing a good connection.

panels.title: Access removed, writes refused, bad messages (per minute)
panels.description: revoked: open connections closed because someone's access was removed. dropped: edits refused (for example from a viewer). bad: malformed messages, whose socket is closed.

panels.title: Browser metric events refused
panels.description: Browser reports the server rejected as invalid. Should be 0; above 0 means a buggy or hostile client.

panels.title: Messages per second, by kind
panels.description: What clients send. sync_update is edits, awareness is cursors and presence, ping is the latency probe, sync_step1/2 are the connect handshake.

panels.title: Time to process one message
panels.description: Server time to handle a client message (role check, apply the edit, fan out). Measured in the gateway, so it excludes the network.

panels.title: Size of edit messages
panels.description: Bytes in messages that carry edits. Large values mean big pastes or full-state syncs.

panels.title: Time to store one edit in the database
panels.description: MongoDB write time per edit. Rising values are the first sign the database is struggling.

panels.title: Database write failures and compactions (per minute)
panels.description: failures: edits the database refused (the room retries and nothing is lost while the gateway stays up). compactions: merging the edit log into a snapshot.

panels.title: Rooms with unsaved edits over time
panels.description: Should stay at 0. Any rise lines up with a database outage.

panels.title: Relay messages per second
panels.description: Edits passed between gateways. Only exists when more than one gateway runs.

panels.title: Relay trouble and self-repair (per minute)
panels.description: errors: Redis failures. reconnects: the subscription coming back after being lost. resyncs: rooms re-reading the database to repair edits missed while the relay was down (reason 'reconnect' right after an outage, 'periodic' every 60 s as a safety net).

panels.title: Requests per second, by route
panels.description: Busiest API routes (route patterns, so no document ids appear here).

panels.title: Slowest routes (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile response time for the busiest routes.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(synapse_http_request_duration_bucket[$__rate_interval]))) and on (route) topk(6, sum by (route) (rate(synapse_http_request_duration_count[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: 2xx fine, 3xx not modified, 4xx a client problem (sign-in needed, no access), 5xx a server fault.

panels.title: Sign-in failures and rate limiting (per minute)
panels.description: auth: wrong passwords and bad tokens. rate limited: requests refused for coming too fast. A spike can mean password guessing.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of ONE core used by the server process (1.0 = a full core).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Memory held by the server process. Grows with open documents.

panels.title: Event loop delay (p99)
panels.description: How late the server runs scheduled work. The earliest sign a Node server is overloaded: above ~100 ms people feel lag.
